title: The Latest Crier for Mar 31, 2026
items:
Front Row with Harry Smith: A Night to Remember with a New York Philharmonic Quartet

Front Row with Harry Smith, a Pella Corporation and Central College speaker series, welcomes a piano quartet comprised of members of the New York Philharmonic. 
7 p.m. Tuesday, March 31 Douwstra Auditorium. 

Doors open at 6:30 p.m. Concert is free and open to the public. 

Harry Smith, 1973 Central graduate and trustee, will emcee this interactive and instructive special concert. Chamber music performed by members of the New York Philharmonic will include Mozart, Beethoven, Brahms and more.

Free Home-Cooked Lent Breakfast! Last 2!!

Last 2 Lent Breakfast of the year! Join us Wednesday, 3/25 & 4/1 from 7 to 7:45 am in the Lower Chapel to enjoy a devo & home-cooked breakfast made by local churches!

Interested in Kinesiology?

Group Advising for current freshmen planning to major or minor in Kinesiology will take place on Tuesday, March 31, 2026 in HJHC 104. Please attend one of the sessions below to plan your fall 2026 course schedule.- 11:00am-11:30am = Pre-Health Interest (AT, Chiro, OT, PT, etc.) - 11:30am-12:00pm = Physical Education or Exploring Kinesiology

Benefit Bash Ticket Sales

Benefit Bash tickets are officially on sale—starting TODAY! 🎉 Grab yours early for a chance to win extra raffle prizes and be part of an unforgettable evening supporting the Marion County Humane Society. 

Stop by our table in Maytag today from 11 AM–1 PM to get your ticket and learn more about the event! Tickets are $5. 

Can’t make it today? No worries—we’ll be back in Maytag on Monday, March 30 and Tuesday, March 31 from 11 AM–1 PM. You can also swing by Student Development anytime to purchase your ticket. 

Don’t miss out on a fun night for a great cause! 🐾

Got questions? President Putnam has answers April 9th!

Come to the Presidential Forum, hosted by Senate! April 9th | 8pm | VSC 180 
Open to all Central students and staff, come with concerns or questions to discuss with President Putnam.

Speaker James Suong, Cambodian Refugee and U.S. Army Veteran, Tues., April 7th, 11:00am

Mark your calendars now! You are invited to come hear the story of James Suong, a child survivor of the Khmer Rouge "killing fields" over 50 years ago and now a 30-year U.S. military veteran currently serving as the senior human resources specialist for the Iowa Army National Guard. How did he get from there to here? What can we learn from him, and by extension, other immigrant stories as well? Find out at 11:00am, Tuesday, April 7th, in Van Emmerik Studio in Maytag. Then join Mr. Suong and History Club for lunch in the Market siderooms afterwards.

SECRET CHURCH: livestream teaching by David Platt, Pizza, & Snacks!

Many Christians around the world cannot study God’s Word without severe persecution. Join us for Secret Church on April 17th as we study the book of Elijah, word by word & pray for believers persecuted in Nepal with teaching by David Platt over the course of 6 hours. Livestream begins at 6:00 pm & food is provided starting at 5:30pm. Dinner, snacks, livestream, & booklet are provided, just make sure to reserve your spot today! Please email laflinh@central.edu with questions. Sign up here to secure your spot: 
https://forms.gle/STimLbTZauRWWQCB6

Trade Snow for Sun: Merida, Mexico (Jan 4–15, 2027)

Looking for an unforgettable way to spend Winter Break? Join our faculty-led trip to Merida, Mexico ( January 4–15, 2027 ), and immerse yourself in the language, culture, and everyday life of the Yucatan Peninsula. 

Enroll in SPAN 160/260/360/460 – Language & Culture in Yucatan (1–4 credits) during Fall 2026 , and travel with the class to Merida, Mexico over winter break in January 2027 for an immersive cultural and language experience. 

No matter your Spanish level, this course invites you to engage deeply with local culture, strengthen your language skills, and explore one of Mexico’s most vibrant and historic cities. 

Interested? Contact Prof. Oscar Reynaga (reynagao@central.edu) for more information.

Intro to Statistics (MATH 105) offered online this summer

In case you’re needing credits, an EXP3 course, or need MATH 105 for your major/minor, you’re in luck as MATH 105 is offered this summer! MATH 105: Intro to Statistics will be offered online this summer from 6/1-8/7 and will be a fully asynchronous course. There will be deadlines along the way, lots of virtual office hours, but also lots of flexibility in completing the course over the summer. Please note though, MATH 105 is a 4-credit course with a healthy workload. 
If you have questions or want more information, email goodmanr@central.edu .

Signup for Softball now! 

Email wisemans@central.edu with any questions you may have. Events may be contingent upon weather and number of team registrations.

Speaker James Suong, Cambodian Refugee and U.S. Army Veteran. April 7th. 11:00am

Mark your calendars! Tuesday, April 7th, 11:00am in Van Emmerik Studio . Just over 50 years ago, James Suong was a child in Cambodia running from the horror of the Khmer Rouge's "killing fields." He and his mother succeeded, and now he is a 30-year U.S. military veteran. He is coming to campus to tell the remarkable story of how he got from there to here. Learn about his journey from war refugee to immigrant to U.S. citizen and military officer. You are also invited to lunch afterwards with Mr. Suong in Market siderooms 105/106.
